 L-R: Tom Hanks and Meg Ryan in 'You've Got Mail,' Jason Orley 
 Warner Bros/Alida Wuenscher 
 EXCLUSIVE: What would You’ve Got Mail look like decades on from the heyday of AOL? We’re about to find out, as Warner Bros. is developing a new take on the classic romantic comedy, with Jason Orley aboard to direct.
 Details as to the take are being kept under wraps. Orley, the filmmaker behind I Want You Back and Big Time Adolescence , is writing the current draft based on a screenplay by Deborah Kaplan & Harry Elfont ( Can’t Hardly Wait , Josie and the Pussycats ).

 Coming off the 20th rom-com Beach Read , based on Emily Henry’s bestseller, Neal Moritz is producing alongside Tania Landau via Original Film .
 Directed by Nora Ephron, You’ve Got Mail stars Meg Ryan and Tom Hanks as an independent children’s bookshop owner and the corporate bookselling magnate threatening her livelihood who become pen pals online, falling for each other without realizing they’re rivals.
 Watch on Deadline 
 Based on Miklós László’s play Parfumerie and its film adaptation The Shop Around the Corner , the rom-com captured the emergence of email as a medium for intimacy, long before dating apps were around, and spoke to the ’90s trend of big-box bookstores squeezing out independent shops. It released via Warner Bros. in December 1998 and grossed over $250M worldwide.
 The film marked the third pairing for Hanks and Ryan, following Joe Versus the Volcano and Sleepless in Seattle , and the duo’s final film with the beloved Ephron.
 Orley comes to You’ve Got Mail after wrapping post on his third feature, an Amazon comedy titled Close Personal Friends that stars Brie Larson, Jack Quaid, Lilly Collins and Henry Golding. Maximum Effort produced alongside Isaac Aptaker and Elizabeth Berger, from a story conceived by Orley and Aptaker.
 Previously, Orley collaborated with Aptaker and Berger on the romantic comedy I Want You Back , which he also directed for Amazon and which stars Charlie Day, Jenny Slate and Gina Rodriguez. His debut feature, the Pete Davidson comedy Big Time Adolescence , premiered in dramatic competition at the 2019 Sundance Film, where it was acquired by Hulu. Also known for work alongside Davidson on his Peacock show Bupkis and assorted comedy specials, he is repped by UTA, Rise Management and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller.
 No strangers to the rom-com, Kaplan & Elfont are known for writing and directing Can’t Hardly Wait and Josie and the Pussycats , as well as writing the films Made of Honor and Leap Year . Creative partners since meeting at NYU’s Tisch School of the Arts, they set up two films at Paramount last year: the R-rated comedy Guys with No Friends , which was acquired in a bidding war, and the Dave Bautista rom-com The Romantic .
 Kaplan and Elfont are repped by Entertainment 360 and Verve. Kaplan is also repped by Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern; Elfont by Hansen, Jacobson, Teller.

 For all those dissing remakes, this itself is a clear “remake” of The Shop Around the Corner (as they say in the article!!) and a better one, imo, than the original move that was inspired by the play. They reference it in the movie clearly with the name of the bookshop. 
 I’m hoping this remake is similarly able to transform the movie for modern sensibilities. It’s one of my favorites in its “cute” factor of the classic 90/00s rom coms but like most of them, there’s a handful of cringe moments that don’t stand up to the modern eye. And with many Barnes & Nobles going the way of the dodo, too, the concept is hard to translate to a new audience.
 Anyway, I’m excited for the update of the concept. Remakes make total sense for this genre and I, for one, and looking forward to it.
